questions.question: What gives Helena hope that she can cure the King?

options.text: Her father's tested medical prescriptions.
Bertram's experience treating wounded soldiers.
Lafew's promise to become the royal physician.
The Countess's discovery of a new medicine.

questions.explanation: Helena inherited remedies from her physician father, including one suited to the King's illness.

evidence.exact:
HELENA.
I will tell truth; by grace itself I swear.
You know my father left me some prescriptions
Of rare and prov’d effects, such as his reading
And manifest experience had collected
For general sovereignty; and that he will’d me
In heedfull’st reservation to bestow them,
As notes whose faculties inclusive were
More than they were in note. Amongst the rest
There is a remedy, approv’d, set down,
To cure the desperate languishings whereof
The king is render’d lost.

questions.question: How does the Countess respond to Helena's proposed journey to cure the King?

options.text: She orders Helena to abandon her father's remedies.
She supplies help and gives Helena her blessing.
She insists that Helena remain at Rossillon.
She sends Bertram to attempt the cure instead.

questions.explanation: The Countess offers permission, attendants, resources, and prayers for Helena's attempt.

evidence.exact:
COUNTESS.
Why, Helen, thou shalt have my leave and love,
Means and attendants, and my loving greetings
To those of mine in court. I’ll stay at home,
And pray God’s blessing into thy attempt.
Be gone tomorrow; and be sure of this,
What I can help thee to, thou shalt not miss.

questions.question: What reward does Helena ask the King to promise if she cures him?

options.text: Ownership of the Countess's estate at Rossillon.
A place among the King's royal relations.
Marriage to an eligible man under his authority.
Command of the French troops in Florence.

questions.explanation: Helena asks to choose a husband whom the King has the power to bestow, excluding the royal family.

evidence.exact:
HELENA.
Then shalt thou give me, with thy kingly hand
What husband in thy power I will command:
Exempted be from me the arrogance
To choose from forth the royal blood of France,
My low and humble name to propagate
With any branch or image of thy state;
But such a one, thy vassal, whom I know
Is free for me to ask, thee to bestow.

questions.question: Why does Bertram initially object to marrying Helena?

options.text: He believes she has already married Parolles.
He thinks she has refused to cure the King.
He has promised to marry Lafew's daughter that day.
He considers a physician's daughter beneath his rank.

questions.explanation: Bertram objects to Helena's birth, and the King answers that virtue can confer honor.

evidence.exact:
BERTRAM.
But follows it, my lord, to bring me down
Must answer for your raising? I know her well;
She had her breeding at my father’s charge:
A poor physician’s daughter my wife! Disdain
Rather corrupt me ever!

questions.question: Where does Bertram go rather than settle into married life with Helena?

options.text: To serve the Duke of Florence in the war.
To accompany the King on a pilgrimage.
To inherit Diana's property in Paris.
To manage his mother's household at Rossillon.

questions.explanation: The gentlemen report that Bertram has gone to serve the Duke of Florence.

questions.question: What conditions does Bertram set before Helena may call him her husband?

options.text: She must cure his mother and leave France.
She must obtain his ring and bear his child.
She must restore the drum and win a battle.
She must gain a title and double his estate.

questions.explanation: His letter demands both the ring he wears and a child fathered by him, conditions he presents as impossible.

evidence.exact:
[Reads.] When thou canst get the ring upon my finger, which never shall come off, and show me a child begotten of thy body that I am father to, then call me husband; but in such a “then” I write a “never”.
This is a dreadful sentence.

questions.question: What role does Helena arrange for Diana in the secret nighttime encounter?

options.text: Persuade Parolles to come instead of Bertram.
Refuse the meeting and return every gift.
Arrange the meeting but let Helena take her place.
Warn Bertram that the King is hiding nearby.

questions.explanation: Helena asks for Diana's apparent consent while Helena occupies her place and Diana remains absent.

evidence.exact:
HELENA.
You see it lawful then; it is no more
But that your daughter, ere she seems as won,
Desires this ring; appoints him an encounter;
In fine, delivers me to fill the time,
Herself most chastely absent. After,
To marry her, I’ll add three thousand crowns
To what is pass’d already.

options.text: He can recognize every soldier through a blindfold.
He would rather die than discuss his own army.
He has secretly commanded the enemy's troops.
He will betray military secrets to save his life.

questions.question: Why does the ring on Bertram's hand alarm the King near the end?

options.text: It belonged to Helena and raises fears she was harmed.
It proves Bertram has stolen the crown of France.
It identifies Bertram as a soldier of the enemy.
It shows that Lafew has broken a marriage promise.

questions.explanation: The King recognizes Helena's ring and fears that Bertram's hatred of her may conceal violence.

evidence.exact:
KING.
Now, pray you, let me see it; for mine eye,
While I was speaking, oft was fasten’d to it.
This ring was mine; and when I gave it Helen
I bade her, if her fortunes ever stood
Necessitied to help, that by this token
I would relieve her. Had you that craft to ’reave her
Of what should stead her most?

evidence.exact:
KING.
Thou speak’st it falsely, as I love mine honour,
And mak’st conjectural fears to come into me
Which I would fain shut out. If it should prove
That thou art so inhuman,—’twill not prove so:
And yet I know not, thou didst hate her deadly.
And she is dead; which nothing but to close
Her eyes myself, could win me to believe
More than to see this ring. Take him away.

questions.question: What does Bertram promise when Helena returns and asks him to accept her?

options.text: To challenge the King to settle their disagreement.
To love her if she clearly proves her account.
To leave France without hearing her explanation.
To marry Diana regardless of Helena's evidence.

questions.explanation: Bertram says he will love Helena dearly if she makes the truth of her claim clear.

evidence.exact:
